positive.prompt: Make this page responsive and WCAG compliant.
Build an accessible modal component with keyboard support.
Refactor the dashboard into reusable components with sane state management.
Rework this profile page so it feels production-quality without abandoning our design system.

negative.prompt: Review this proposed checkout flow before engineering starts.
Use DevTools to diagnose why this already-built button ignores clicks.

evals.prompt: Build a dropdown menu component for the existing design system. It contains user actions, must work on mobile, and should handle loading, no available actions, disabled actions, and an action failure. Use the repository's current frontend stack and prove the result works.
evals.expected_output: A design-system-aligned command menu with semantic controls, complete keyboard and focus behavior, responsive placement, realistic states, focused tests, and concrete runtime verification evidence.
expectations: The repository framework, component conventions, tokens, primitives, state patterns, tests, and runtime commands are inspected before implementation
A semantic button and an appropriate menu interaction pattern are used rather than a clickable generic element or mismatched select semantics
Keyboard navigation covers opening, moving among actions, activation, Escape dismissal, and focus restoration
Accessible names, roles, expanded and disabled states, focus visibility, and non-color state cues are implemented
Loading, empty, disabled, failure, and success behavior are meaningful and recoverable where applicable
Long labels, narrow mobile layout, tablet, desktop, and wide behavior are considered using project breakpoints or representative viewports
Existing design tokens, primitives, spacing, typography, icons, and interaction patterns are reused
Focused unit or component tests and live-browser checks are treated as complementary evidence
The final report names the commands, routes, viewports, states, and keyboard paths actually verified
failure_conditions: Adds a UI, state, icon, browser, or accessibility dependency without proving the current stack is insufficient and obtaining authorization
Claims the dropdown rendered correctly, passed accessibility tooling, or worked in a browser without runtime evidence
Forces React, Tailwind, or a specific browser tool onto a repository that uses another stack
Introduces arbitrary gradients, rounded cards, spacing values, or placeholder copy instead of following the existing product design
